xs-ssh(1) ​

SSH & remote helpers

Choose a shell, prepare the remote helper, and bound idle connections.

DESCRIPTION ​

xsync transports its native protocol over a remote shell, normally OpenSSH. Paths are carried as protocol data. The helper must support the client’s protocol and requested capabilities.

EXAMPLES ​

Use a specific SSH identity
sh
xs -azP -e "ssh -i ~/.ssh/backup_key" src/ user@host:/backup/
Use a different SSH port
sh
xs -azP -e "ssh -p 2222" src/ user@host:/backup/
Bracketed IPv6 host
sh
xs -aP src/ "user@[::1]:backup/"

An empty remote path, host:, refers to the remote current directory. Leading ~ and ~user expand on the server; quote remote wildcards to prevent your local shell from expanding them.

HELPER LOOKUP ​

Transfers try xs on remote PATH, then ~/.local/bin/xs, then XSYNC_REMOTE_PATH. The local environment value takes precedence over the remote value.

Choose an explicit helper
sh
xs -azP --rsync-path=/opt/bin/xs src/ user@host:/backup/
NOTE

An explicit --rsync-path bypasses automatic lookup. If fallback is needed, that same command must support rsync. An explicit xs-only executable may therefore prevent fallback.

EXPLICIT REMOTE INSTALL ​

Install the matching release at ~/.local/bin/xs
sh
xs --install user@host

The install command probes the remote OS and architecture and chooses the matching release artifact. Existing newer or unrecognized versions are refused unless --force is given. This requires matching release binaries to be available locally.

NOTE

Starting a transfer never uploads or silently installs a helper.

BANDWIDTH AND TIMEOUTS ​

Limit bandwidth and remote idle time
sh
xs -azP --bwlimit=10M --timeout=60 src/ user@host:/backup/

Bare bandwidth numbers are KiB/s. Suffixed rates accept binary and decimal units; 0 disables the limit. Compression limits serialized wire bytes remotely; local workers share a limit on bytes written.

--timeout bounds remote idle I/O, including shell/hello waits, partial frames, blocked writes, and a helper that remains alive after protocol EOF. 0 disables it. Local copies have no remote I/O deadline. A timeout exits with code 30.

PROTOCOL AND FALLBACK ​

Protocol 4 supports protocols 4 and 3. Optional features are negotiated before use. Missing helper support, incompatible protocols, and unsupported flags can delegate to rsync before transfer. --no-fallback fails instead.

See compatibility for fallback boundaries and environment for remote-shell precedence.
